headline: Collins St Value Fund sees CSL as a psychological arbitrage opportunity after a 64% drawdown, arguing headwinds are cyclical not structural
reasoning: CSL has suffered a perfect storm of negatives since August 2025: two earnings downgrades, abrupt CEO removal, a US$200M Medicare Part D pricing headwind, severe albumin pricing pressure from Chinese VBP, over 40% impairment of the Vifor acquisition, aggressive competitor ASP discounting of 15-20%, and channel-stuffing inventory resets worth US$300M. Despite this, Collins St argues CSL's core Behring division retains structural moats — it is the global plasma market leader with ~28% fractionation share, highest plasma yield, lowest cost per litre, and gross margins 10-12 percentage points above nearest competitor Grifols. The key catalyst for re-rating is Grifols' own Capital Markets Day guidance signalling a shift away from irrational discounting toward market-growth-aligned volumes and margin expansion ahead of a potential US plasma business IPO, suggesting the pricing headwind is cyclical and set to subside within 12 months. With CSL now trading at what the fund describes as trough multiples versus a historical 30-40x earnings range, Collins St believes the stock offers a highly asymmetric opportunity to buy a moat-entrenched compounder at fire-sale prices.
quote: Off the back of a perfect concoction of bad news in the form of downgrades, industry headwinds, capital allocation woes and abrupt management changes, we believe CSL offers investors a highly asymmetric opportunity for precisely this psychological arbitrage. The stock sold off from its 52-week high of ~$276 to $98 today, a jaw-dropping 64% drawdown for a stock once widely viewed as infallible. The question for our global fund was simple: Do CSL's troubles represent permanent structural impairment, as the daily headlines suggest? Or merely a cyclical downturn mispriced as permanent structural erosion, offering our global fund a rare chance to buy a high-quality, moat-entrenched business at fire-sale prices? We believe CSL at today's price represents the latter.
episode_title: CSL: A psychological arbitrage opportunity

headline: CSL's Vifor acquisition described as arguably one of the worst in Australian corporate history, with over 40% of the ~US$11.7B purchase price impaired
reasoning: CSL acquired Vifor in 2022 for approximately US$11.7B at 18x trailing EBITDA, right at the top of its industry cycle. The segment, which markets intravenous iron and a nephrology portfolio, has required over 40% impairment and has been a persistent drag on management attention, distracting Behring's R&D flywheel and contributing to market share losses. Collins St views this as a capital allocation disaster that compounded the company's other cyclical difficulties.
quote: CSL Vifor was acquired in 2022 for ~US$11.7B at 18x trailing EBITDA right at the top of its industry cycle. The segment markets intravenous iron and a nephrology portfolio. To put it kindly, this acquisition has proved nothing short of a capital allocation disaster... having now impaired >40% of its only recently acquired Vifor business – arguably one of the worst acquisitions in Australian corporate history.

headline: Collins St sees plasma/Ig sector normalising with structural demand tailwinds intact despite near-term cyclical disruption from competitor discounting and policy uncertainty.
reasoning: The plasma industry is characterised as a structural oligopoly with long-term demand growth, currently experiencing cyclical disruption from Grifols' aggressive discounting strategy. With Grifols now pivoting toward margin expansion, the fund expects industry pricing to normalise and CSL's Ig franchise to return to mid-single-digit annual growth. The fund views the current environment as a cyclical trough rather than a structural inflection point for the sector.
quote: Despite being burdened by the perfect storm of transitory issues likely to subside within the next 12 months, CSL still represents a high-moat franchise in an oligopoly industry with structural demand tailwinds. As CSL's main competitor has now signalled the conclusion of its irrational and unsustainable discounting in the near-term, the picture becomes clear that the recent headwinds plaguing CSL are cyclical rather than structural.

headline: U.S. flu vaccine policy uncertainty under RFK Jr creates material near-term headwind for CSL's Seqirus division — Collins St assumes no recovery in base case.
reasoning: The appointment of RFK Jr as U.S. Health Secretary has created uncertainty around U.S. flu vaccine policy, directly weighing on CSL's Seqirus division. Collins St takes a conservative stance by assuming no recovery in Seqirus in its valuation base case, treating this as a potential long-running headwind rather than a near-term cyclical issue. Despite this, the fund still finds CSL attractively valued on the strength of its plasma franchise alone.
quote: We conservatively assume no recovery in CSL's Seqirus division, another segment impacted by a cyclical downturn given U.S. flu vaccine policy uncertainty associated with RFK Jr's appointment as US Health Secretary.

headline: Grifols' Capital Markets Day signals end of irrational Ig price discounting, supporting the view that CSL's pricing headwinds are cyclical rather than structural
reasoning: Grifols had been growing its Ig segment at mid-teens annually in 2024-2025 via aggressive 15-20% ASP discounting, well ahead of the 6-8% end-market demand growth rate, indicating clear market share gains from CSL. However, at its recent Capital Markets Day, Grifols explicitly guided to moderating U.S. Ig growth back to 6-8% from FY26 onwards and announced a focus on expanding group EBITDA margins from 24.8% in FY25 to 29-30% by FY29 ahead of a potential IPO of its U.S. plasma business. Since plasma comprises over 85% of Grifols' group earnings, this margin expansion is incompatible with continued deep discounting, confirming that the pricing pressure on CSL is unsustainable and set to subside within 12 months.
quote: Our thesis is backstopped by Grifols' recent Capital Markets Day, where an explicit guidance of moderated U.S. Ig growth in line with the broader market of 6-8% from FY26 onwards was issued. Additionally, Grifols openly signalled its shift in focus to expansion of group EBITDA margins from 24.8% in FY25 to 29–30% by FY29 as it gears up for a potential IPO of its U.S. plasma business. Given Grifols' plasma segment comprises >85% of group earnings, this margin expansion cannot be achieved as the company continues to torch ASP with double-digit discounts. As CSL's main competitor has now signalled the conclusion of its irrational and unsustainable discounting in the near-term, the picture becomes clear that the recent headwinds plaguing CSL are cyclical rather than structural.

headline: U.S. Medicare Part D redesign under the Inflation Reduction Act mechanically reset immunoglobulin pricing 20% lower, creating a structural US$200M revenue headwind for plasma manufacturers
reasoning: The Inflation Reduction Act's Part D redesign permanently restructured U.S. Medicare-funded immunoglobulin pricing, resetting it 20% lower under a new manufacturer discounting regime. This created a US$200M headwind for CSL's FY26 revenues and represents a one-time regulatory re-basing of pricing rather than an ongoing deterioration in demand fundamentals. Collins St treats this as an industry-wide headwind that is now largely absorbed into trough earnings estimates.
quote: The company, and industry at large, was also hit with a permanent U.S. Medicare restructuring via the Inflation Reduction Act's Part D redesign. This mechanically reset U.S. Medicare-funded immunoglobulin pricing 20% lower under a new manufacturer discounting regime causing a US$200M headwind for CSL's FY26 revenues.

headline: Chinese government volume-based centralised procurement has structurally weakened albumin per-unit economics across the plasma industry
reasoning: Albumin, previously a higher-margin product for plasma manufacturers, experienced severe pricing pressure across the industry as Chinese government VBP initiatives drove down per-unit economics. This is characterised as a structural change to that sub-segment rather than a cyclical fluctuation, representing one of the multiple concurrent headwinds that combined to create the negative sentiment spiral around CSL.
quote: Albumin also experienced severe pressure across the industry as Chinese government volume-based centralised procurement initiatives structurally weakened the per-unit economics of what was previously a higher margin franchise.
